result.rationale: The diff shows Admin::EmbeddingController#update does nothing except re-serialize via fetch_embedding: it never reads params or persists anything, yet renders a success response. The client saveChanges calls embedding.update({}) — also with no data. So the shipped PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint returns 200 while silently discarding any changes; this is verifiable directly from the controller code in the diff.

judged_text: The update action is a silent no-op: it re-renders the embedding without reading params or persisting anything, and the saveChanges action in admin-embedding.js.es6 that calls embedding.update({}) has no trigger in any template. PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns 200 success while changing nothing, so the next developer who wires a save button to the existing saveChanges action, or any API client that PUTs embedding changes, ships a feature that silently fails to save.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` and does not read `params` or persist anything (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`). On the client, `admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`, but `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs` has no button/action wired to `saveChanges`, so this path is currently unused. This is a real, diff-grounded incompleteness/misleading API surface (PUT exists but is a no-op), but it doesn’t break existing behavior in the shown UI since host CRUD is handled via `EmbeddableHostsController`.
